title: Black Friday vs. Cyber Monday: Which day should you shop for the best deals?
summary: Should you shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday? Here's which day is better for deals and how to score the best ones in 2026.
content: Once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza. The lines really began to blur when the world shut down in 2020, and brick-and-mortar stores hosted online sales in lieu of in-person Black Friday events. In 2026, lines outside stores are practically nonexistent. We certainly can't see them. While major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on big-ticket items (like TVs , Apple devices , smartwatches , headphones , and of course, Amazon's own devices ) . That includes discounts that beat Amazon's massively hyped October Prime Day deals. SEE ALSO: Everything to know about Black Friday 2026: Best deals, sale dates, how to shop smart, and more If you're debating when you should start adding big-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place. After years of covering both sales extensively, here's our expert analysis. Black Friday vs. Cyber Monday — what's the difference? Way back in the age of MySpace and AIM — aka 2005 — the National Retail Federation debuted the term "Cyber Monday" after realizing that the Monday after Thanksgiving saw a flood of online sales. This was likely due to shoppers using their faster internet connections at work on Monday morning to snag deals, or at least that's what they credited it to. That, of course, and the fact that online retailers wanted some of that holiday shopping bread, too. Thus, two distinct deal-shopping days were born: Black Friday, for those who wanted to shop in stores the day after Thanksgiving, and Cyber Monday, for those who preferred shopping from the comfort of their desks. Over 20 years later, there's little — if any — real difference between the two due to the alleged " death of retail ." Everyone and everything is online, so why wouldn't Black Friday be? Based on our years of experience covering both, we can truly say neither is a "better" day to shop. It really comes down to what you're looking for and how much demand there is for it. Are there better deals on Black Friday or Cyber Monday? If you see a solid deal, grab it, no matter which sale title it falls under. There's not a tremendous amount of distinction anymore in terms of discounts on particular products, as there was in previous years. However, there are still rules to follow in some product categories: TV deals tend to be more dramatic and widespread for Black Friday, with a higher likelihood of selling out before the clock even turns to Cyber Monday, while waiting for Cyber Monday to double-check that there's not a new, better laptop deal is often wise. But with the blurred lines of Cyber Week, many of these deals will cross over. As noted at BlackFriday.com , "Some TV deals will feature flashy discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but they might not have the specs you're after." TL;DR: The deals will be great for both shopping days, but it all depends on what you're looking for. If you see specs you like listed under a product at a price you like, grab it to be safe. How long is Black Friday? Black Friday proper falls on Nov. 27 in 2026, but it's honestly silly to even call it Black Friday at this point. It's no longer just on Friday — it's a month-long affair. You can shop deals at practically every retailer starting right after Halloween (before, even), with most labeling something an "early Black Friday deal" as early as November. Best Buy's official early Black Friday sale kicked off Nov. 6, while Target's began on Nov. 5 . Amazon's actual Black Friday sale starts Nov. 19, but you can already find the "early Black Friday deal" tag on plenty of listings. In other words, if you want to get some early shopping done, have at it. Once the clock strikes midnight on Friday, it's basically Cyber Monday (yes, even though it's actually Saturday). We don't make the rules. The deals won't change too much, but the search terms and official site banners will. When do Cyber Monday deals start? Officially, Cyber Monday is on Monday, Nov. 30 in 2026. Unofficially , it basically starts the second Black Friday ends, with retailers calling sales "Cyber Monday" deals as early as Saturday, Nov. 28. So basically, semantics — and it's easier to just think of the Cyber Week language as interchangeable.

title: Disney+ and Hulus Black Friday deal is live — get both for under $5 per month
summary: Through Nov. 30, new and eligible returning subscribers can get the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu Bundle for $4.99/month for 12 months (down from $12.99/month), or go ad-free for $14.99/month.
content: TL;DR: Through Nov. 30, new and eligible returning subscribers can get the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu Bundle for $4.99 per month for 12 months (down from $12.99), or go ad-free for $14.99 per month (down from $21.99). Opens in a new window Credit: Disney / Hulu Disney+ and Hulu Bundle: $4.99/month for Black Friday Get Deal at Disney+ If your monthly streaming bills have quietly crept up this year, Black Friday is easily the best window to reset them. Right now, Disney+ and Hulu are running their biggest bundle promotion of the year — slashing 12-month Duo plans by up to 61% for new and eligible returning subscribers through Nov. 30. Unlike typical streaming promos that only discount the cheapest ad-supported tier for a couple of months, this offer locks in promotional pricing for a full 12 months across both the ad-supported and ad-free Duo plans. Here's how the two Black Friday tiers break down: Disney+ and Hulu Bundle (With Ads) — $4.99/month for 12 months (regularly $12.99/month — save $8/month, or $96 over the year) Disney+ and Hulu Bundle (No Ads) — $14.99/month for 12 months (regularly $21.99/month — save $7/month, or $84 over the year) Both bundles give you full access to Disney+ , Pixar , Marvel , Star Wars , National Geographic, Hulu Originals , next-day fall TV , and movies , plus select live ESPN College Football games and College GameDay on Saturdays inside Disney+. You can stream through both standalone apps or watch select Hulu content directly inside the Disney+ app (up to two simultaneous streams for Hulu content via Disney+), with 4K UHD and Dolby Atmos support on compatible titles, parental controls, and Disney+ Perks included. If you spring for the Premium tier, you also get offline downloads and ad-free viewing across most on-demand titles (though ads still appear in select live and linear programming). SEE ALSO: TikTok creators are joining Disney+ as Hulu integration wraps up Before you sign up, there are a few important eligibility rules and billing caveats to keep in mind. The deal is open strictly to U.S. residents ages 18 and older who are new or eligible returning subscribers — if you currently have an active Disney+, Hulu, ESPN, or bundle subscription, you will not qualify on that account. The offer cannot be stacked with free trials, other promos, or gift cards, and switching plans after redeeming forfeits the promotional rate. There is no annual lock-in, so you can cancel anytime (cancellations take effect at the end of your current billing period, with no refunds or credits for partial months), though once your 12-month promotional year wraps up, your plan will automatically renew at the regular monthly rate ($12.99 or $21.99 per month, or the then-current regular price) unless you cancel beforehand. Grab whichever tier fits your streaming habits at Disney+ before the Black Friday bundle pricing ends on Nov. 30.

Originally created by engineer Josh Wardle as a gift for his partner, Wordle rapidly spread to become an international phenomenon, with thousands of people around the globe playing every day. Alternate Wordle versions created by fans also sprang up, including battle royale Squabble , music identification game Heardle , and variations like Dordle and Quordle that make you guess multiple words at once . The entire archive of past Wordle puzzles was originally available for anyone to enjoy whenever they felt like it, but it was later taken down , with the website's creator stating it was done at the request of the New York Times . However, the New York Times then rolled out its own Wordle Archive , available only to NYT Games subscribers. Is Wordle getting harder? title: My skin loves the Shark CryoGlow red light mask — its on sale for nearly $100 off during Black Friday
summary: A coupon on Amazon brings the Shark CryoGlow down to $255 during Black Friday. A Mashable expert talks about why it's worth every penny.
content: Save 27%: As of Nov. 27, the Shark CryoGlow LED face mask is down to $255 at Amazon, thanks to an on-page coupon. This brings the price down $94.99 from $349.99, and far beats the discount at nearly every other retailer, where the red light mask is on sale for $299.99. Opens in a new window Credit: Shark Shark CryoGlow LED face mask $255 at Amazon $349.99 Save $94.99 With on-page coupon Get Deal at Amazon I currently have a gorgeous cystic breakout right in the middle of my cheek (skin knows when you're seeing a bunch of family), and the singular thing keeping me from pulling out my Shark CryoGlow mask is that I'm at my folks' for a couple of days. SEE ALSO: Black Friday 2026 live: Best deals, store hours, free giveaways, and real-time updates If I had stayed even one night more to celebrate the holiday, I would've performed miracles to fit the LED light mask into my suitcase (I am, unfortunately, a chronic overpacker), as it is simply that game-changing for my skin. I've been religious about my skincare routine for a long time, and after seeing aestheticians and dermatologists, I generally have a handle on my dehydrated, oily, and acne-prone skin. But when it comes to giving my skin glow, smoothing out my fine lines, and most importantly, zapping stubborn acne, the Shark CryoGlow is my favorite tool in my skincare arsenal. And for Black Friday, it's down to its best price ever at $255, knocking an impressive $94.99 off the $349.99 list price, thanks to an on-page coupon at Amazon. You just can't be picky about the color — the deal only applies to the lilac colorway. Date in my camera roll: December 2025. I've been a fan. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable More proof! Both that I use this mask and that I'm addicted to photographing myself in it for fun. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable My former colleague Leah Stodart explained all the tech around what makes the Shark mask so great (and why it's the best LED light mask our team has tried ), but I'll give you the quick version: It features blue, red, and near-infrared light, meaning it can treat a variety of skincare concerns from acne to anti-aging It legitimately calms and clears my breakouts faster and more reliably (more so than the Solawave wand or Bye Acne device ) My skin gets smooth after using this mask consistently The built-in timer and remote make it easy to make using it more of a habit at the beginning or end of my day The cooling eye pads feel like heaven The hard shell mask fits my face better than other red light masks (though a flatter design is more ideal for travel) It's significantly more affordable than other major red light masks, even at full price. For $255, it's nearly unbeatable Though the Shark mask is an investment and not essential to a skincare routine, it makes a great gift to a loved one (that includes yourself!) and gives you the ability to have a skincare spa day at home, even if you only have eight minutes or so to spare. title: Kohls is giving away free Kohls Cash and Sephora coupons for Black Friday — how to claim this weekend
summary: Kohl's is handing out free $5 to $100 Kohl's Cash vouchers on Black Friday (Nov. 27) and $5 to $100 Sephora coupons on Saturday (Nov. 28) to the first 200 shoppers at each store.
content: TL;DR : Kohl's is giving the first 200 shoppers at each store a free $5 to $100 Kohl's Cash voucher on Nov. 27 (at 5 a.m.) and a $5 to $100 Sephora coupon on Nov. 28. Opens in a new window Credit: Kohl's Free $5–$100 Kohl's Cash and Sephora at Kohl's Coupons Get Deal at Kohl's If you are looking to score free spending money for your holiday shopping run, Kohl's is giving early birds two big reasons to set an alarm this Black Friday weekend. For the first time ever, the retailer is pairing its classic Black Friday morning Kohl's Cash giveaway with a second wave of free Sephora at Kohl's coupons on Saturday, Nov. 28 — plus a four-day sweepstakes with $10,000 cash grand prizes. Kohl's stores are closed on Thanksgiving Day (Nov. 26) , though its main Black Friday Week sale is already live online. When physical stores reopen for the weekend, each giveaway comes with its own timing and same-day redemption rules, so here is how to claim yours. Nov. 27: Free Kohl's Cash starting at 5 a.m. Most Kohl's locations open bright and early at 5 a.m. local time on Black Friday, Nov. 27, though exact hours can vary by store. The first 200 customers through the doors at each participating Kohl's location will receive a free, instant Kohl's Cash voucher worth $5 to $100 — no purchase necessary. However, you have to spend the promotional voucher in stores on that same day, and standard exclusions apply (it cannot be used on Sephora at Kohl's merchandise or gift cards). SEE ALSO: Kohl's Black Friday 2026: See the ad and shop early deals Nov. 28: Free Sephora at Kohl's coupons If you would rather sleep past 5 a.m. on Friday — or you are mainly shopping for beauty gifts — Kohl's is running a second in-store giveaway on Saturday, Nov. 28. For the first time, the first 200 shoppers in line at participating Sephora at Kohl's locations will get an instant promotional coupon worth between $5 and $100 off at Sephora at Kohl's. Just like Friday's doorbuster, the Sephora coupon is handed out on a first-come, first-served basis when doors open (limit one per household for shoppers 18 and older) and must be redeemed toward in-store beauty purchases that same day. Be sure to check your local Kohl's store page before heading out, since Saturday opening hours differ from Friday's 5 a.m. doorbuster schedule and not every Kohl's houses a Sephora shop. SEE ALSO: Black Friday 2026 deals: The best store freebies from Kohl’s, Target, Lowe’s, and more Nov. 27-30: Enter Kohl's $10,000 sweepstakes Even if you skip the early-morning lines altogether, you can still enter Kohl's Black Friday sweepstakes from 5 a.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 27 through 11:59 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 30. You can submit a free entry either in stores or online — no purchase required — as long as you are 18 or older and live in the U.S. (limit one entry per person). title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 28, 2026
summary: See the Moon phase expected for November 28, 2026 as well as when the next Full Moon is expected.
content: The Moon is looking noticeably less full now, although most of its surface is still illuminated. We're still in the Waning Gibbous phase, with the Moon getting a little smaller each night as we head towards the Third Quarter. What is today's Moon phase? As of Saturday, Nov. 28, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 81% of its surface visible. If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Oceanus Procellarum, as well as the Tycho Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Gassendi Crater, the Clavius Crater, and the Archimedes Crater. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11 and 15 landing spots, plus the Fra Mauro Highlands. When is the next Full Moon? In North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24. What are Moon phases? It takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA . Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a New Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit. Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

content: Best Black Friday headphones deals at a glance: Best headphones deal overall Bose QuietComfort Ultra (1st gen) $229 (save $200) Get Deal Best budge pick Sony WH-CH530 $38 (save $31.99) Get Deal Best premium deal Sony WH-1000XM6 $348 (save $111.99) Get Deal Another great option under $200 Sony WH-1000XM4C $198 (Save $101.99) Get Deal Black Friday headphones deals started out strong earlier this month, but now that it's actually Black Friday, they're even better. Take, for instance, the 45% discount on the second-generation Bose QuietComfort headphones ( released just this past August, btw ). Prefer a flagship model? No problem, the Sony WH-1000XM6 — our top pick for premium sound — are over $100 off . SEE ALSO: Everything to know about Black Friday 2026: Best deals, sale dates, how to shop smart, and more As someone who tests headphones year-round and is heading into her sixth year covering Black Friday at Mashable, I only write about deals that are actual deals. That means double-checking accurate list prices, using my price history knowledge from looking at headphone product listings every time I open my work laptop, and consulting the Mashable shopping team's collective knowledge of historical pricing. This year, my criteria also include an awareness of price increases that have affected nearly every area of tech. With all that in mind, those two aforementioned deals — and the ones below — are the best headphones deals you'll find on Black Friday. If and when any more notable deals drop, you'll be sure to find them on this list. Best Black Friday headphones deal overall Opens in a new window Credit: Bose Bose QuietComfort Ultra (1st gen) $229 at Woot $429 Save $200 Get Deal at Woot Why we like it It's basically impossible to beat the value of this Bose deal, which brings the first-generation Ultras down to a record-low price of $229. Not only is that a $200 markdown — it's $120 cheaper than the next-gen Ultras, which have minimal differences from the first-gen option. In other words, if you're looking for flagship performance at mid-range prices, this is the deal to get. Best Black Friday budget headphones deal Sony WH-CH530 $38 at Amazon $69.99 Save $31.99 Get Deal at Amazon Why we like it You don’t have to spend Bose money for a pair of everyday headphones. At $38, the Sony WH-CH530 offer up to 55 hours of battery life, multipoint Bluetooth for connecting to two devices at once, and a quick-charge feature that gets you another 90 minutes of listening after just three minutes plugged in. These are on-ear headphones, and they don’t have active noise cancellation, so they’re better suited to shoppers who want an inexpensive pair for music and taking calls. These headphones also hit the market just this past September , and at $38, are already matching the record-low of their predecessor and a former budget favorite of ours, the Sony CH-520N . Best Black Friday premium headphones deal Sony WH-1000XM6 $348 at Amazon $459.99 Save $111.99 Get Deal at Amazon Get Deal at Sony Why we like it The Sony WH-1000XM6 are our top pick for premium sound , and the discount makes their flagship price a little easier to stomach. Mashable’s testing found improved sound quality, particularly on vocal-heavy tracks, along with excellent active noise cancellation and a comfortable fit for longer listening sessions. Sony also brought back the folding design, so these are easier to pack than the XM5s. Battery life hasn’t improved from the previous generation, but you still get up to 30 hours with ANC on. At $348, these headphones are down to a record-low price, beating their former sale price of $378 that we already recommended picking up. In other words, you're not likely to grab a much better deal than this if you've been waiting on buying Sony's flagship headphones. Portable power stations have been in high demand this year, so it's well worth shopping sale models during Black Friday. Since we're seeing unpredictable weather, it's smart to grab one of these sale models to be better prepared. Come summer weather, take the power station camping to keep small devices charged. Our power station expert, Lauren Allain, gave it 4.5 stars and a Mashable Choice Award after spending two weeks using it to charge her devices and run appliances, including a rice cooker, blender, and air fryer. Between a global RAM shortage driven by the AI boom, which pushed Sony to hike console prices twice in under a year, and the massive hype around GTA 6 , standalone console markdowns are nowhere to be found. Today, the PS5 Slim Digital Edition starts at $599.99, and the flagship PS5 Pro retails for $899.99. Depending on the model, that means PlayStation 5 hardware actually costs $150 to $200 more today than it did when the console originally launched in 2020. For weeks, the hype around GTA 6 completely wiped out store shelves across the country — especially for the PS5 Pro . The good news is that major retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Amazon are finally restocking standard PS5 models at regular list price. We recommend paying full sticker price, because third-party marketplace listings are barely worth looking at anyway — the few that are up are mostly refurbished units marked up to nearly double the retail cost, so we left them off our list. PS5 vs. PS5 Pro — which restock should you grab? Even at full sticker price, picking up a PS5 or PS5 Pro makes a lot of sense if you are upgrading for GTA 6 or catching up on Sony's massive library of current-gen games. The standard PlayStation 5 Digital Edition gives you the core current-gen experience in a slim, compact design that fits easily into a media console. You get an 825GB ultra-high-speed SSD that cuts load screens to seconds, 4K TV output, up to 120 fps gameplay on supported titles, and Tempest 3D AudioTech. It also ships with Sony's DualSense wireless controller — featuring haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that add physical resistance when you pull a trigger or drive over rough terrain — and plays more than 8,500 backward-compatible PS4 games with smoother frame rates. Plus, if you ever decide you want to buy physical discs later, you can snap Sony's detachable disc drive right onto the side. SEE ALSO: Black Friday PlayStation deals are selling out fast: Shop games, controllers, headsets on sale If you want the best possible visuals in Vice City, stepping up to the PlayStation 5 Pro unlocks PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) for sharper AI-upscaled clarity, upgraded GPU performance, and advanced ray tracing. While Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 targets 30 fps across all consoles at launch, the PS5 Pro is the only system that gets exclusive ray-traced shadows and cleaner image upscaling in the game. Beyond GTA 6 , dozens of major PS5 titles run at higher frame rates and sharper resolutions on the Pro, and its massive 2TB SSD easily swallows GTA 6 's 212GB install size with plenty of storage left over for the rest of your library. Where to find the PS5 and PS5 Pro right now If you want to lock down a console while shelves still have stock, here is where the PS5 Digital Edition and PS5 Pro are currently available at standard retail price: Amazon — Along with the standalone PlayStation 5 Digital Edition and PlayStation 5 Pro 2TB available at regular retail price, Amazon also has the PlayStation 5 Digital Edition (825GB) + DualSense Wireless Controller Bundle discounted by roughly $22 — the only actual bundle discount floating around major stores right now. Best Buy — Both the PlayStation 5 Digital Edition and the PlayStation 5 Pro 2TB are available to order online right now at list price. Target — You can grab both the PlayStation 5 Digital Edition and the PlayStation 5 Pro 2TB at standard retail price while current restocks last. Walmart — The PlayStation 5 Digital Edition is back in stock directly from Walmart at regular retail price. Where to actually save on PS5 hardware If you don't want to pay 2026's inflated brand-new sticker prices, look straight at PlayStation Direct's certified refurbished lineup . Sony sells official refurbished PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles for up to $100 less than brand-new units ($499.99 for the Digital Edition, $549.99 for the Disc Edition, and $849 for the PS5 Pro), backed by a full one-year manufacturer's warranty. It is the most reliable way to shave real money off the console without gambling on sketchy third-party resellers. You might also spot occasional game bundles at big-box stores, though availability is hit-or-miss. Even the overpriced bundles and double-the-price third-party listings floating around online are largely sold out, proving just how intense the demand still is. title: The 17 best Black Friday TV deals: Get a 65-inch OLED for $799 and save 50% with doorbuster deals
summary: Black Friday TV deals are live at Amazon and Best Buy. Grab a 65-inch OLED TV for $799 or a budget set starting at just $68.
content: Savvy TV shoppers wait all year to buy TVs during Black Friday , and the best Black Friday TV deals are now live. Best Buy has several one-day-only doorbuster TV deals, Walmart has a budget set starting at just $68, and we found 50% discounts on both OLED and QLED TVs at Amazon . So, whether you're buying a cheap TV for a spare guest room or splurging on the Samsung S95H OLED TV (our tech editor's dream TV), we've searched through hundreds of Black Friday TV deals to curate this guide. You can also follow our Black Friday live blog to be the first to know about new deals and price drops. The best Black Friday TV deals at a glance: Best TV Deal Overall Roku 65-inch OLED Pro Series 4K RokuTV $799.99 (save $400 at Amazon) Get Deal Best 43-inch TV Deal Amazon Ember 43-inch 4-Series Fire TV $199.99 (save $130 at Amazon) Get Deal Best 55-inch TV Deal Insignia 55-inch Class QF Series QLED 4K Fire TV $169.99 (save $230 at Best Buy) Get Deal Best 65-inch TV Deal Hisense 65-inch E7 Mini-LED Hi-QLED 4K TV $499.99 (save $500 at Amazon) Get Deal Best 75-inch TV Deal TCL 75-inch QM8L SQD-Mini-LED QLED 4K TV $1,397.99 (save $1,602 at Amazon) Get Deal best premium OLED TV deal LG 65-inch C6 Series OLED 4K TV $1,399.99 (save $1,300 at Amazon) Get Deal Best Micro RGB TV Deal Sony 65-inch Bravia 7 II True RGB 4K Google Gemini TV $1,499.99 (save $1,100 at Best Buy) Get Deal Best Budget TV Insignia 40-inch F40 Series LED HD Fire TV $84.98 (save $65.01 at Amazon) Get Deal Best Super-Budget TV onn 32-inch LCD HD TV $68 (save $20 at Walmart) Get Deal The Ultimate Splurge Samsung 65-inch S95H OLED 4K TV $2,299.99 (save $1,100 at Best Buy) Get Deal SEE ALSO: Black Friday streaming deals 2026: The best deals live now and what's still to come Our tech experts will be closely monitoring prices on the best TVs of 2026 throughout Black Friday to find the best deals from brands such as TCL, Samsung, Hisense, Amazon Fire TV, LG, and more. We'll also compare prices across the most popular retailers to make sure you're truly getting the best possible price. Remember: a new TV is a great Christmas gift idea the whole family will appreciate, and this is your chance to save. Need some guidance? Check out Mashable's guide to TV specs for a quick refresh on the difference between QLED, OLED, mini-LED, and RGB displays. Roku 65-inch OLED Pro Series 4K TV This fall, Roku's new OLED TVs have been selling out at Amazon, and that was before they got a $400 price drop. This TV isn't as bright or sleek as Samsung or LG's best OLED TVs, but it's right in the sweet spot for affordability, letting you enjoy deep blacks and dazzling colors without spending over $1,000. This is also a great TV for gamers, and our colleagues at CNET recently gave it a Lab Award for having the "Lowest Input Lag" in their tests. Opens in a new window Credit: Roku Roku 65-inch OLED Pro Series 4K TV $799.99 at Amazon $1,199.99 Save $400 Get Deal at Amazon Hisense 65-inch E7 Mini-LED Hi-QLED 4K TV Even as every other tech product gets more expensive, new TVs are seemingly immune to the price hikes we've seen in recent years. Case in point: You can get the 65-inch Hisense E7 QLED TV for $499.99 at Amazon, a full 50% discount from its retail price. This is the lowest price ever for this TV, according to our research. Get fast access to your favorite streaming apps via the Fire TV OS, and take advantage of the 144Hz refresh rate for watching movies and playing video games. The bottom line: While this discount is available, this smart TV offers high-end features at a budget price tag. These budget TV sets essentially double as Alexa+ smart speakers, and despite the low price, you can still enjoy 4K content on an HDR10+ display. Both the 43-inch and 55-inch models are 39% off now that Amazon's Black Friday TV deals are live. The best Black Friday TV deals always include discounts on the latest model, and the new C6 offers incredible peak brightness, dark blacks, and expansive colors, now with an AI processor for smoother motion and upscaling. Pull out a microscope, and you'll find 8.3 million self-lit pixels. Our favorite OLED TV for most people just keeps getting cheaper. We saw the 65-inch LG C6 OLED TV drop to just $1,499.99 during Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days event in October, but now it's $230 less and at a record low on Amazon , according to our research. The result is a TV with a picture that jumps off the screen and colors that pop even in a bright living room. For those who want a 75-inch TV that can be the centerpiece of a home theater, this QLED TV has remarkable blacks and bright colors, with brightness that puts OLED competitors to shame. Whatever you call them, RGB TVs use red, green, and blue miniature LED backlights (as opposed to just white and blue) for more accurate color and contrast. And Sony’s True RGB technology , introduced in May, sets a very high standard. If you want a future-proofed TV that combines the benefits of OLED and QLED, then grab Sony's new Bravia 7 II True RGB flagship TV while it's more than $1,000 off at Best Buy. Besides the gorgeous display, this TV has a sleek design with thin bezels, and for AI power users, it brings Google Gemini right into your living room. Opens in a new window Credit: Sony Sony 65-inch Bravia 7 II True RGB 4K Google Gemini TV $1,499.99 at Best Buy $2,599.99 Save $1,100.00 Get Deal at Best Buy Samsung 32-inch Movingstyle Essential 4K Smart Monitor Can't decide between a new monitor or new TV this Black Friday? The 32-inch monitor can be wheeled from room to room, and can be used without a computer like a regular TV. Though the stand is heavy when setting up, the wheeled setup and 13 feet of power cord make it easy enough to move from space to space. title: I found 36 of the best Black Friday phone deals on iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, and more
summary: The best Black Friday phone deals save shoppers up to $600 on unlocked Apple, Google Pixel, Samsung Galaxy, Motorola, and Nothing devices.
content: The best Black Friday phone deals: Best unlocked iPhone deal Apple iPhone Air (256GB) $799.99 (save $300) Get Deal Best unlocked Samsung Galaxy phone deal Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 (256GB) $1,499.99 (save $400) Get Deal Best unlocked Google Pixel phone deal Google Pixel 11 Pro (256GB) $749 (save $350) Get Deal Best unlocked Motorola phone deal Motorola Razr Ultra 2025 (512GB) $699.99 (save $600) Get Deal Best unlocked Nothing phone deal Nothing Phone (4a) Pro (128GB) $397.99 (save $102) Get Deal This holiday season, the best Black Friday phone deals help offset the price hikes that have affected almost every brand. A new phone is more expensive these days, but it's easy to avoid paying full price if you shop strategically. In fact, you might pay as little as $0 by upgrading through your carrier. The only catch is that their deals typically require a trade-in and a lock-in to an extended contract. For a new phone with no strings attached, go the unlocked route instead. Retailers like Amazon and Best Buy are currently discounting unlocked smartphones from Apple, Samsung, Google, Motorola, and Nothing during their Black Friday sales . After spending a few hours combing through their deals, I've identified three dozen good ones that can save you up to $600. Whether you want a new phone that takes incredible pictures, offers multi-day battery life, flips, folds, or comes in well under $500, you've got plenty of options. Best iPhone deal Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple iPhone Air (256GB) $799.99 at Best Buy $1,099.99 Save $300 Get Deal at Best Buy The ultra-thin iPhone Air is the best choice "for minimalists and aesthetes who care more about their phone's looks than its performance," to quote my iPhone buying guide . It's not the fastest or longest-lasting iPhone, nor does it have the best cameras, but it is a gorgeous phone. (Mashable's Senior Editor Stan Schroeder called it "the sexiest iPhone I've ever tested.") Thanks to Best Buy, the base model now costs $100 less than the standard iPhone 17 ; it's usually $200 more. Note that the iPhone Air's MagSafe Battery pack is also on sale for 40% off this Black Friday. Read Mashable's full review of the Apple iPhone Air. He was also impressed by its powerful Snapdragon chipset. Its "50MP wide and 50MP ultrawide cameras are fine, but not elite," he noted, but that's frequently the case with foldables. (Creators and mobile photographers should look into the Galaxy S26 Ultra instead — or the Google Pixel 11 Pro, below.) Based on my research, Amazon's Black Friday price of $1,499.99 for the base Galaxy Z Fold 8 is an all-time low. Read Mashable's full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. title: Zelda Switch 2 restock: Live restock updates at Walmart, Target, and Best Buy (Nov. 28)
summary: Looking for the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2? Here is today's live stock update across Target, Best Buy, Walmart, and more retailers.
content: Where to check for Zelda Switch 2 stock: Nintendo Nintendo Switch 2 — The Legend of Zelda — 40th Anniversary Edition $519.99 at Nintendo Shop Now Amazon Nintendo Switch 2 — The Legend of Zelda — 40th Anniversary Edition $519.99 at Amazon Shop Now Walmart Nintendo Switch 2 — The Legend of Zelda — 40th Anniversary Edition $519.99 at Walmart Shop Now Target Nintendo Switch 2 — The Legend of Zelda — 40th Anniversary Edition $519.99 at Target Shop Now Best Buy Nintendo Switch 2 — The Legend of Zelda — 40th Anniversary Edition $519.99 at Best Buy Shop Now GameStop Nintendo Switch 2 — The Legend of Zelda — 40th Anniversary Edition $519.99 at GameStop Shop Now If your current morning ritual involves violently hitting refresh on a dozen retail tabs, you already know the vibe: finding the Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition is turning into an Olympic sport. We're closely monitoring inventory at all the major retailers and are cautiously optimistic it will be restocked for the holiday shopping season. On the question of if/when the limited-edition Zelda Switch 2 will be restocked, a Nintendo spokesperson provided this not-entirely-reassuring statement to Mashable: "Although we cannot provide detailed information, we are striving to ensure that we can supply our products to those who want them." Between automated bot armies scooping digital drops, surprise order cancellations at Walmart, and inventory vanishing in seconds on Amazon, this custom black-and-gold console feels like a myth. But while digital storefronts look completely barren, stock is actively circulating behind the scenes. Where to check for Zelda Switch 2 stock right now Before getting into the restock details, bookmark these retailer pages to check for surprise drops: Nintendo Store — Out of stock right now, but you can add it to your wishlist to get pinged the second a restock hits. Amazon — Dropping tiny batches of consoles randomly throughout the day. Walmart — Stock exists but only for third-party listings selling at way over market price, so make sure your in-stock email alerts are turned on. Target — Sold out online, but periodic drops have taken place in-store. Best Buy — Sold out online, but select stores ran midnight openings on Nov. 5 with walk-in stock. GameStop — Online orders are off; you will have to walk into a store to find one. Why is the console selling out so fast? The feeding frenzy is being supercharged by Nintendo’s staggered release calendar. While the custom Zelda 40th Anniversary hardware dropped first on Oct. 29, the flagship game driving demand — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 — arrived on Thursday, Nov. 5. The remake rebuilds the 1998 classic from the ground up with modernized controls, a fully orchestrated soundtrack, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments. Since the $520 console doesn’t include the game, everyone is rushing to lock down a system before launch day. Opens in a new window Credit: Nintendo The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 $59.99 at Amazon Shop Now at Amazon What comes with the Zelda 40th anniversary Switch 2? The package includes the special-edition Switch 2 system sporting a custom black-and-gold finish, themed Joy-Con 2 controllers, and a matching dock decorated with the gold Triforce emblem. It retains the platform's signature flexibility, letting you switch between TV , Tabletop, and Handheld modes whenever you want. Inside the themed chassis, you get 256GB of built-in storage (expandable with microSD Express cards), a vivid display in handheld mode, faster load times, and support for up to 4K resolution on compatible TVs when the console sits in the dock. The magnetic Joy-Con 2 controllers add mouse-style tracking in supported games, while the new GameChat hub lets you voice chat and share your screen directly as you play. It also plays your older Switch games and supports standard multiplayer options. How can you improve your chances of finding stock? Landing limited-edition Nintendo hardware takes a little prep work, but these battle-tested habits will give you a real edge over the bots: Save your checkout details everywhere — Log in to Target, Best Buy, Walmart, and the Nintendo Store to save your shipping address and default card. Stopping to type a card number or billing zip code during a live drop is how you lose an order. Hands off the refresh button in Best Buy's queue — When an online drop goes live, Best Buy puts shoppers into a randomized waiting line to filter out scrapers. Touching the reload button resets your spot and boots you straight to the back. Watch for Walmart+ early-access paywalls — Walmart frequently locks headline console drops behind paid Walmart+ subscriptions for the first 30 to 60 minutes. If you have a membership, keep that tab signed in; if not, wait for the general public window to unlock. Dodge third-party sellers — Double-check the seller before buying. Marketplace scalpers frequently list units for jacked-up prices; make sure it says "Sold and shipped by [Retailer]" at the standard price. Skip the web wars and head to physical stores — Online checkout bots grab website stock in under 15 seconds. Showing up in person is easily your most reliable path to securing one without paying scalper markups. Will the Zelda Switch 2 be restocked on Black Friday? Hopefully, yes, but this hasn't been confirmed. Stores like Walmart, Amazon, and Best Buy often hold onto popular gaming hardware to use as headline deals during Black Friday and Cyber Monday week. With that said, Black Friday restocks are usually the hardest ones to catch. You will be fighting website crashes, gift shoppers, and automated bots all at once. If you can grab a console whenever stock appears, take it. Think of Black Friday as a backup plan, not your main bet. Console hunting sucks right now, period. But between the surprise micro-drops and physical store restocks, you still have real shots at retail price — just be ready to move the second that stock goes live.
